# Examples

Runnable projects live in the
[`examples/`](https://github.com/markurtz/git-versioned/tree/main/examples) folder of the repository. Each one's README is
its test: the commands in it run on every test run, in a fresh copy of the
folder, and must print what the README shows.

See [Use Cases](use-cases.md) for every use case and the example that
shows it.

## Example Index

### Beginner

| Example                                                                                                                  | Shows                                                                                                                         | Needs       |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------- |
| [Hatchling, zero config](https://github.com/markurtz/git-versioned/tree/main/examples/hatchling)                         | A Python package whose version comes from git tags at build time, with nothing configured.                                    | git, Python |
| [setuptools from pyproject.toml](https://github.com/markurtz/git-versioned/tree/main/examples/setuptools)                | A setuptools package versioned from tags, with settings and scopes in `pyproject.toml`.                                       | git, Python |
| [setuptools from setup.cfg and setup.py](https://github.com/markurtz/git-versioned/tree/main/examples/setuptools-legacy) | Older setuptools layouts: settings in `setup.cfg` and a `setup.py` that only calls `setup()`.                                 | git, Python |
| [Every version shape](https://github.com/markurtz/git-versioned/tree/main/examples/version-shapes)                       | Release, dev, dirty, nightly and pre-release versions in PEP 440 and SemVer, with the settings and variables that shape them. | git, Python |
| [Pull request titles and commit messages](https://github.com/markurtz/git-versioned/tree/main/examples/commit-checks)    | `check` validates titles, commit ranges and commit-msg hook files against the allowed types and scopes.                       | git, Python |

## Try one

```bash
cp -r examples/hatchling /tmp/hatchling && cd /tmp/hatchling
git init -q && git add -A && git commit -qm "feat: first version"
git tag v1.2.3
gitversioned version
```

## Run the example tests

```bash
hatch run project:tests-e2e
```
